references.text: Ezekiel describes how God sends his arrows of famine against the people, using the same imagery of arrows as instruments of God's judgment.
Lamentations mentions how God uses arrows against his people, parallel to God's arrows as punishment.
The psalmist describes God's deadly weapons and burning arrows that he prepares against the wicked.
David laments that God's arrows have struck him, using the same image of God's judgment.
It speaks of the arrow that flies by day and the plague that walks in darkness, contrasting with protection from God's judgment.
Job describes how the arrows of the Almighty have struck him, using the same imagery for God's punishment.
Later in the same chapter, the image is expanded with God's arrows drinking blood and swords devouring.
God warns that more plagues will be gathered upon the people through disobedience, addressing the same theme of accumulating disasters.
Jeremiah conveys that God has determined four kinds of punishments for the people, parallel to gathering calamities.
Ezekiel mentions God's four severe punishments: sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague, elaborating on gathered disasters.
